$\text{Slope}=\dfrac{\text{Rise}}{\text{Run}}=\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}$

We can calculate the change in $x$ and change in $y$ by picking any two pairs of corresponding $x$- and $y$-values.

$\begin{array}{lrrrr}
&&\xrightarrow{+5}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+5}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow{+5}\,\,\,\,
\\
x
&-4
&1
&6
&11
\\
\hline
\\
y
&-3
&-2
&-1
&0
\\
&&\xrightarrow[+1]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[+1]{}\,\,\,\,
&\xrightarrow[+1]{}\,\,\,\,
\end{array}$

So the slope is:

$\dfrac{\text{Change in }y}{\text{Change in }x}=\dfrac{1}{5}$

question.content:
